blocks.text: Ada Tours is not responsible for missed hotel breakfasts when you check out early for a flight or an excursion.

Your driver will meet you at the airport and take you to your hotel. You can spend the rest of the day by the ocean or explore the city on your own.

Copacabana, Ipanema and Leblon are known for their wide beaches and black-and-white mosaic promenades. From early morning until late evening, people play football and volleyball on the sand, open-air cafés serve coconut water, fresh juices and other drinks, and local musicians perform. Between the buildings, you catch glimpses of the ocean and green slopes. Even a stroll along the seafront gives you a feel for how the city fits into its landscape.

For a more active day, Rio offers golf, tennis, surfing, rafting, diving, hang gliding and more. With green hills, bays and islands all around, you can spend your first free day on the beach, walking along the ocean or getting to know the city’s neighborhoods at your own pace.

After breakfast, you’ll set out on a four-hour sightseeing tour.

First you’ll go up Urca Hill, where the lookout has a restaurant and bar. The cable car then takes you to Sugarloaf Mountain, with views of Copacabana, the bay, the surrounding mountains, the islands, the Niterói Bridge and the statue of Christ on Corcovado.

After coming back down, you’ll drive into the historic center of Rio. You’ll see old churches and monasteries, the city’s main cathedral and colonial buildings. The day shows you two sides of Rio: its natural setting from above and its historic architecture downtown. From the summit, you can see how bays and mountains divide Rio into distinct neighborhoods. In the center, the focus shifts to façades, squares and the city’s history.
